LESSON: COMPOSITION OF AIR

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: MATTER Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experienc
Topic 2.2: Composition of air
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Composition of air, part of MATTER Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experienc in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does air pollution affect the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm in purposive groups, on the meaning air and its constituent. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views.

2. Draw/trace a pie chart showing percentage composition of components of air in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with fine motor difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, given physical support by peers/learner support assistant to draw. Adapted working surfaces should be

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm in purposive groups, on the meaning air and its constituent. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views.
2. Draw/trace a pie chart showing percentage composition of components of air in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with fine motor difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, given physical support by peers/learner support assistant to draw. Adapted working surfaces should be

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Composition of air together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The learner relates concept of environmental conservation as they discuss on air pollutants and come up with

ways of reducing air pollution in the environment.

● Learning to learn: The learner learns new skills of controlling air pollutants as they explore the school and neighborhood to

identify air pollutants.

16

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner observes safety precautions in an air polluted environment as they identify and discuss methods

of reducing air pollution.

● Patriotism: The learner serves the community by making posters on common air pollutants, dangers of air pollution and ways

of controlling air pollution to educate members of the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-economic and environmental issues (Environmental education and climate change): The learner practices ways of

environmental conservation as they identify and discuss methods of reducing air pollution.

Link to other learning areas

The learner uses mathematical skills to draw a pie chart showing the percentage composition of components of air. .
